findings.claim: The decision reads only each simple command's argv0. Wrapper commands (sudo, time, env, nice, timeout, xargs, command) and command substitution put curl/wget outside argv0, so the new parser allows them through. r3's text is unchanged from r2 on this point; the gap persists.
findings.evidence: v1 regex /(^|\s|&&|\||;)(curl|wget)\s/i matches 'sudo curl -s https://x' and 'echo u | xargs curl -s' but the ADR names no wrapper list and no $(...) rule. Confirmed still true by re-reading ADR-0008 r3 §'Same scope as v1' and change #1/#2: no wrapper or subshell handling is added in r3.
findings.archaeology: INTRODUCED_BY v1 fbf402fd (2026-02-25, 'unified PreToolUse hook — block Bash data-fetching'), refined by 3383299c (2026-03-05, 'Fix false-positive HTTP regex matching inside quoted arguments'). ORIGINAL_INTENT (code comment at routing.mjs:787): regex is deliberately broad ('single-word curl/wget... rare false positive') to catch curl under any wrapper. REGRESSION_RISK: high — an argv0-only AST parser is narrower than v1's string regex, so v2 fails open on common wrappers v1 denied. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: v2 must keep v1's wrapper coverage as a floor (owner: no fallback chain, no regression).
findings.fix: Define a fixed wrapper list (sudo, env, time, nice, timeout, xargs, command, doas) whose first non-flag operand becomes the effective argv0; recurse into $(...), backticks, and the string operand of bash/sh/zsh -c and eval. Add GP3 rows for each.

findings.claim: Change #2's 'allow when the body does not reach stdout' test drops v1's silent-flag and verbose-flag conditions for issue #166. 'curl -o f url' (no -s) and 'curl -s --verbose -o f url' would now be allowed, re-breaking the stderr progress-bar flood #166 fixed.
findings.evidence: v1 routing.mjs:755-762 comment 'Must be silent ... to prevent progress bar stderr flood'; tests/hooks/core-routing.test.ts:178 and :186 require both cases denied. ADR-0008 r3's golden table (GP3) only tests 'curl -sL -o out.bin' (silent) as allow, never the no-silent or --verbose case.
findings.archaeology: INTRODUCED_BY 2731ca25 (2026-03-22, 'feat: allow curl/wget with silent file-output, block stdout floods (#166)'). ORIGINAL_INTENT (commit message, quoted): 'Example blocked: curl -o file url (no -s, progress bar floods stderr)'. REGRESSION_RISK: high, direct re-break of a closed, named issue (#166). SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: 'body reaches tool output' must cover stderr, not only stdout.
findings.fix: Allow file-output curl/wget only when silent (-s/-q, or stderr redirected) AND not verbose (no -v/--verbose/--trace/-D -). Add GP3 rows: 'curl -L -o f url' -> deny, 'curl -s --verbose -o f url' -> deny.

findings.claim: 'ParseError -> allow, journal the code' is fail-open for the user's permissions.deny rules too, not only for the curl/HTTP deny. A command with [[, ((, case, a function, or <(...) that also contains a user-denied pattern (e.g. 'f(){ sudo rm -rf ~; }; f') or curl bypasses both checks, since both read the same parse tree.
findings.evidence: ADR-0008 r3 line 51: 'Constructs the parser does not handle ... raise ParseError(code). Result: allow and journal.' v1 security.ts had a separate extractSubshellCommands path plus CONTEXT_MODE_REQUIRE_SECURITY=1 fail-closed mode (routing.mjs:678-690) precisely because a single parser failing open on the deny check was judged unsafe.
findings.archaeology: Same lineage as ENF-1 (fbf402fd/3383299c) plus v1's security.ts fail-closed escape hatch added later for the deny-policy path specifically. ORIGINAL_INTENT: unparseable constructs must not silently clear the user's own deny rules. REGRESSION_RISK: a user who set Bash(rm -rf:*) deny gets no protection once the command contains a bash idiom the parser can't read. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: no fallback chain (owner decision) — the one path must still check deny rules on unparsed input.
findings.fix: On ParseError, still run a conservative literal-token scan of the raw command against the user's deny patterns and the curl/wget/HTTP lists before allowing; journal only that the structured parse failed, not that no check ran.

findings.claim: ADR-0008 r3's 'Same scope as v1' table lists only the bare 'user permissions.deny -> deny' row and never names ctx_execute, ctx_execute_file or ctx_batch_execute. v1 enforced the same deny rules against those tools at both hook and server layers; a Bash(rm -rf:*) deny is otherwise bypassed by routing the same command through ctx_execute.
findings.evidence: v1 routing.mjs:924-990 (deny checks on ctx_execute/execute_file/batch_execute); server.ts:1746,2122,2127 checkDenyPolicy; security.ts:363-394 auto-reads .claude/settings.json and .claude/settings.local.json with no import step.
findings.archaeology: INTRODUCED_BY b3f93eba, closing an earlier sandbox-as-deny-bypass issue; extended in round-3 (#451) to read every adapter's global settings path automatically. ORIGINAL_INTENT: host deny rules must apply with no separate opt-in, to every tool that runs code or reads a path. REGRESSION_RISK: v2 (PRD G6, policy.json as the declared source) reopens the exact bypass b3f93eba closed. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: host deny rules keep applying automatically; policy.json may only add to them, never replace them.
findings.fix: Add ctx_execute / ctx_execute_file / ctx_batch_execute / ctx_index(path) rows to the ADR-0008 scope table, checked server-side against the host's own deny rules with no import step.

findings.claim: Case B's PreToolUse 'allow' + updatedInput on a subagent Bash call means Claude Code skips the permission prompt entirely, and the rewritten command becomes 'node <bundle>/run.mjs <base64>', so any Bash(...) deny/ask rule and any other hook that inspects the command text no longer sees the real command. A subagent command the user's own permission rules should block or ask about now runs unseen.
findings.evidence: ADR-0016 line 27 text: 'PreToolUse returns allow + updatedInput. The command becomes node <bundle>/run.mjs <base64 of the original>.' This is the same mechanism ENF-4's deny-bypass concern applies to, now for subagents specifically.
findings.archaeology: Related to the same b3f93eba lineage (ENF-4): v1's fix there established that a mechanical rewrite must not itself become an unchecked execution path. ORIGINAL_INTENT: enforcement happens before any rewrite, not after. REGRESSION_RISK: a MUST requirement (ADR-0016) silently removes the user's own Bash permission layer for every subagent command it rewrites. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: no fallback chain; the rewrite path must run the user's deny/ask checks on the original command before constructing updatedInput.
findings.fix: Run the existing deny-policy / curl / HTTP checks against the original command before issuing the case-B rewrite; deny (not allow+rewrite) when the original command would itself be denied or needs an ask prompt.

findings.claim: Budgeted lazy greedy selection sorts candidates by ratio with no tie-break. Equal ratios (same weight, age and size, or two items at age 0 in the same turn) are routine, so 'same rows -> same bytes' depends on sort stability and input order, which the ADR never pins.
findings.evidence: ADR-0009 section 4: 'Take items in ratio order' has no secondary key; section 5 claims '[V] 10 runs out of 10 identical' on one engine, which is not a proof of a stable order across engines or Node versions.
findings.fix: State a total order: ratio desc, then seq desc, compared by integer cross-multiplication (s1*b2 vs s2*b1) so float rounding and sort-stability differences across runtimes cannot change the selection.
